thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager (sev2) — GPU OOMs observed in decode/stream nodes in us-west-2 affecting /v1/stream. Error rate spike at 2310000400. Sample trace ids: trace-8f3a, trace-9b2c. Top impacted customer: AcmeCorp (payment flow).

alex: I’m oncall, taking this. Initial look: multiple decode pods hitting CUDA OOMs in quick succession, ~20% of streaming requests failing with 'CUDA out of memory' and some complete node restarts.

maria: Noted. Do we have a common request pattern? Could be runaway generation or mis-specified max_tokens. Any headers showing unusually large max_tokens?

alex: Pulling logs now. Example request metadata:
```
route: /v1/stream
model: redwood-decode-xlarge
request_id: trace-8f3a
client_headers: {"x-max-tokens": "1000000", "user-id": "acme.payment"}
```
Looks like an upstream client sent a million tokens cap.

sam: That would definitely blow the cache/KV and explode memory over multiple steps. We saw similar when prefix caching grows unbounded. Any churn pattern? Pods OOM then restart and keep taking traffic.

alex: Yes — node flaps observed: kubelet restarted container on 3 nodes in a 3m window. Kubernetes events show oom_kill for process 'runtime-decode'.

maria: Immediate mitigation: add hard cap at ingress/router to clamp max_tokens to a safe upper bound while we fix the model handler. Proposed clamp: 5000 tokens. This avoids relying on client headers.

sam: Agreed. I can apply an Envoy header rewrite rule for the route to set x-max-tokens: 5000 for streaming routes. Will push a quick policy now.

alex: Doing that. Command I used:
```bash
# apply temporary header rewrite
kubectl -n redwood exec -it router-abc -- sh -c '\n  curl -X POST http://localhost:9901/config -d "route:/v1/stream:set_header:x-max-tokens:5000"\n'
```
Pushed at 2310000820. Monitoring...

kira: Heads up — Acme SE is on the phone. They reported timeouts on payment confirmation flows. They've seen 500s in the last 6m. Please let me know customer-facing impact.

alex: Current error rate: 18% 5m err spike on /v1/stream, latency jump to 1.8s p95 from 400ms baseline. We saw drops for ~7 minutes after the first node flapped. Applying header clamp should start reducing new runaway sessions.

maria: Next step: patch the decode runtime to enforce a hard upper bound server-side (in addition to router clamp). I’ll cut a non-disruptive config change that adds MAX_TOKENS_HARD=5000 and a fast rollout (canary -> all). This avoids relying on edge rewrites.

jamie: If we patch the runtime, we should prefer a soft fail mode that truncates the requested generation rather than killing the request, so customer sees partial output rather than resets. Also add a metric tag for 'client_max_tokens' so we can alert on outliers.

sam: While patch is rolling, throttling policy for streaming queues would help. I'll enable per-route concurrency limit from 200 -> 80 to reduce burst memory pressure.

alex: Router clamp in and visible reduction in new large requests. I still see ~3 pods in crashloop from prior OOMs. We should cordon/drain those nodes so they stop receiving new allocations until they’re healthy.

maria: Agreed. sam, can you drain affected nodes? Node names: node-usw2-dec-03, node-usw2-dec-05, node-usw2-dec-09.

sam: Starting drains now. `kubectl drain node-usw2-dec-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` etc. Rebalance in progress.

kira: Customer comms: Acme wants an ETA. Impact: payment confirmations failing for some users for ~12 minutes. Please prepare a short blurb for SE.

maria: Hotfix PR created: runtime: enforce MAX_TOKENS_HARD env var and truncate rather than OOM. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1972. Canary rolling at 2310001100.

alex: Canary looks good for 5m. No further OOMs on canary pods. Rolling to 50% now.

jamie: After 50% roll and validation, roll full. Also capture metrics for truncated responses so we can correlate to customer support tickets. Add an eval check to ensure truncation doesn't break required structured outputs.

sam: Concurrency cap applied. Drained nodes coming back after restarts and kernel memory reclaimed. No new OOMs in last 6m post-clamp.

incident-bot: Post-deploy check: error_rate(/v1/stream) down from 18% -> 2% in 10m, latency p95 back to ~420ms.

kira: Messaging to customer drafted: "We detected large generation requests that exceeded our safety bounds, causing transient failures. We've applied emergency limits and a runtime patch; your traffic should be normalizing. We’ll follow up with a root cause and permanent fix." Should I send?

alex: Send now, ask SE to escalate if they see regressions. Also open an incident ticket for postmortem.

maria: Filed INC-2310 and assigned to eng-runtime for RCA. Root cause hypothesis: client misconfiguration allowed arbitrarily large max_tokens via header; no prior server-side hard cap on streaming decode.

jamie: Action items captured:
- short: router clamp (done), concurrency cap (done), node drains (done), runtime hotfix rollout (done)
- mid: add server-side hard cap permanent + truncation, add alerts for client_max_tokens anomalies, add per-customer token budgeting
- long: tighten API contract validation, add client-side SDK safeguards, update runbook for decode OOMs and automated fallback to quantized variant

alex: Oncall handoff: I'll prepare summary for next shift. @oncall-bot please page night oncall at 2310001800 with summary.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled to @maria-night at 2310001800. Incident ticket INC-2310 created.

sam: Monitoring for 30m. If error rate stays low and no node flaps, we'll close the pager.

kira: Acme SE confirmed they pushed a temporary fix on their side to cap max_tokens; they reported degraded experience but stable.

alex: Closing notes: customer impact contained, mitigation successful. Postmortem required due to customer-facing failures and node restarts. I’ll start the postmortem doc and tag eng-runtime, eng-sre, and support.

jamie: Thanks everyone. Please add any logs/traces to INC-2310. We’ll schedule RCA meeting tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
